Health Care & Nursing Services in India

Health care and nursing services in India — levels, agencies, staffing and the nurse’s role in service delivery.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Describe levels of health care
  • Describe the agencies delivering nursing services
  • Describe the nurse’s role in health services
  • Explain the career ladder for nurses

In simple words

Health services in India are delivered by public and private agencies at three levels. Nursing services are the largest part of the workforce, and the nurse contributes at every level.

Levels of health care

Level Provided by
Primary Sub-centres, PHCs, community outreach, AYUSH
Secondary District and CHC hospitals — internal medicine, general surgery, paediatrics
Tertiary Medical college hospitals, specialty institutes

Agencies delivering nursing services

  • Government hospitals — district, PHC, CHC and teaching hospitals
  • Private hospitals and nursing homes
  • Missionary and voluntary agencies
  • Defence, railways, police and industrial services
  • International agencies — WHO, UNICEF, Red Cross
  • Nursing regulatory bodies — INC and State Nursing Councils

Nurse’s career path

Stage Role
GNM / B.Sc. Nursing Clinical care in ward and community
Post-basic B.Sc. Advanced clinical practice
M.Sc. Nursing Nurse educator, clinical specialist, administrator
Specialisation Critical care, oncology, paediatric, community health
Leadership Ward in-charge, nursing superintendent, matron, principal

🔴 Nurse’s role in service delivery

The nurse is the largest health work force, the patient’s first and constant contact, and the link between doctor, family and community — and she also runs the quality systems of a unit.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Health care levels: primary, secondary and tertiary.
  2. Primary level has PHCs, sub-centres and outreach.
  3. Nursing career starts with GNM or B.Sc. Nursing and goes to M.Sc. and specialisation.
  4. INC sets standards; State councils register nurses.
  5. The nurse is the largest group of health workers.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Districts host CHCs and district hospitals for secondary care.
  2. NGOs and missions extend care to the community.
  3. Specialised training improves critical care and mental health care.
  4. Nursing services are planned by staffing, budgeting and quality control.
  5. Interagency cooperation reduces gaps in the namespace.

📌 Memory trick

Career ladder: G-B-P-M-S-L — GNM, BSc, Post-basic, MSc, Specialisation, Leadership.

60-second revision

  • Levels of care: primary, secondary, tertiary.
  • Agencies: government, private, NGO, missions, industrial.
  • Nursing staff run wards, ICUs and community clinics.
  • Career: GNM to B.Sc. to M.Sc. to specialist and leadership.
  • INC sets standards; state councils register.

Test yourself

A private nursing home provides care at which level?

Answer: B. Private nursing homes provide secondary level care, after primary level health care.

Primary health care in India is delivered mainly through:

Answer: B. Primary health care is delivered through sub-centres and primary health centres with outreach.

The largest group of health workers in a hospital is:

Answer: B. Nurses constitute the largest workforce and deliver most of the direct care.

Which body registers nurses in the state?

Answer: B. Registration is with the State Nursing Council; the INC sets standards of education and practice.

A ward in-charge has mainly a role in:

Answer: A. A ward in-charge supervises, allocates staffing and monitors care and records in the unit.
